newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania halts merchant fleet privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Romania halts merchant fleet privatisation.

text.p: Romania on Friday halted privatisation of its merchant fleet to stop fraudulent takeovers of vessels, many of which are impounded overseas, Transport Minister Traian Basescu said.
"We have to determine the fleet's real situation," Basescu told a briefing during a cabinet meeting devoted to revising the 1997 budget to meet International Monetary Fund demands.

"We have to stop fraudulent privatisation of the fleet. Some private shipping companies operating fleet vessels have abandoned them with the intention of recouping them later at lower prices through other companies."

Basescu said the meeting had allocated $13.9 million from the State Ownership Fund (FPS) to secure the release of dozens of Romanian ships impounded in foreign ports for failing to pay harbour mooring and other outstanding debts.
"The government has intervened as the ships are considered Romanian teritory," he said. "We also wanted to avoid subjecting crews to serious situations."
Romanian media often broadcast reports of merchant seamen stranded in foreign ports with no food or money and reduced to seeking help from local people.
Basescu said the government had withdrawn the licences of 10 private shipping companies earlier this year on grounds that they had failed to operate their vessels properly.

Basescu said that within the next month 31 ships owned by three state-owned companies, Navrom, Romline and Uzinexport, would be repatriated on a "commercial basis" -- by negotiating repayment of debts or seeking out new shipping contracts.
Earlier this month, the Transport Ministry persuaded the state-run bank Bancorex SA to grant one of the companies credits worth $4 million to free the ships.
